chips.title: Lifecycle core on the command line
chips.summary: The merged client, service, event log and execution grants support a complete choice through Markdown and terminal review.

evidence.message: Commit 314ba02 delivered the core. Six CI jobs passed on Windows, macOS and Linux with Node 20 and 22. Each job starts its own test service.

chips.title: D1 · Choose the first release’s request kinds
chips.summary: Record which kinds ship in phase 1 and which move to phase 2. Include the effect of adding side-by-side blind comparisons.

evidence.message: Review 0002 asks the person to choose between choices and approvals, all everyday kinds, and adding blind comparisons.
D1 is waiting for a choice between all everyday kinds, choices and approvals only, or all everyday kinds plus blind comparisons and their review page.
Phase 1 ships choices, approvals, manual steps, clarifications, result checks, assumption lists and FYI notices. Side-by-side blind comparisons ship in phase 2.

chips.title: D4 · Decide what an unanswered request allows
chips.summary: Record when dependent work waits and whether a reversible default is allowed. Apply the answer to default claims and later corrections.

evidence.message: Review 0002 contains the options and the panel’s recommendation. The decision record contains an answer to the earlier review only.
D4 chose defaults for small decisions with a one-step undo, plus a panel before larger technical defaults.

chips.title: D5 · Choose where people answer reviews
chips.summary: Record the default channel for a single question and a batch, including any size cutoff and whether the review page moves into phase 1.

evidence.message: Review 0002 asks the person to choose chat, a page, or a split by batch size.
D5 chose chat for one or two questions and a phase 1 review page for batches of three or more. Terminal review worked well for decisions without visuals.

chips.title: D6b · Confirm who maintains blind comparisons
chips.summary: Record whether UTP takes over the existing comparison pages. Combine this answer with D1 when scheduling any move.

evidence.message: Review 0001 kept the integration plan. Review 0002 asks for confirmation after defining blind comparison.
D6b chose to move existing comparison workflows to UTP when side-by-side blind comparisons ship in phase 2.

chips.title: Publish the decisions from review 0002
chips.summary: Record all four answers, update the phase scope and adjust the board dependencies for any review page or blind comparisons selected for phase 1.

evidence.message: The concept phase closes when the public decision record includes the outstanding answers. Other settled work can proceed independently.
UTP presented D4, D5 and D6b together in the terminal. Publishing waits for those answers. D1 was recorded in conversation.
All four choices are recorded. UTP verified D4, D5 and D6b in the terminal. The public decision record and phase updates can now be prepared.
Published all four decisions and updated the release scope. Batch review pages ship in phase 1. Blind comparisons and migration ship in phase 2.

chips.title: Keep decision history searchable after relinking
chips.summary: Relink two idle projects. Searches from the new project must show the old project’s decisions and reversals with their origin. Archived records stay read-only.

evidence.message: The client checks both projects and updates the checkout mapping. The existing end-to-end test covers a fresh clone. Verify refusal with open work or grants on either side.
Relinking preserves searchable decisions and reversals with their origin after restart. Archives are read-only, and open work on either side prevents relinking.

chips.title: Run one shared decision service
chips.summary: Deploy the service with persistent storage and connect clients on the intended private network. A request made on one machine can be answered on another.

evidence.message: Decision D2 selected a shared service. The automated suite starts a temporary service. An inventory found no listener on the documented port.
UTP runs on the home server and reloads reviews after restart. SSH terminal access works. Direct cross-machine clients still need verification.
On the private network, Windows filed a test request, macOS answered it, and Linux read the same decision from the persistent service.

chips.title: Verify recovery against the latest authorization
chips.summary: Exercise competing owners, revisions, withdrawals and narrowed answers around execution. After interruption, any new grant covers only the authorized work still outstanding.

evidence.message: The verification plan covers zero, partial, different and unknown effects, recovery fingerprints, ownership changes and the risk of a paused owner resuming.
Tests cover withdrawal, narrowed scope, old records and takeover. Partial recovery must match the current authorization before another grant can issue.

chips.title: Verify the shared log on all three operating systems
chips.summary: Run real clients against the same service on Windows, macOS and Linux. Verify checkout identity, restart recovery, concurrent writers and exactly-once retries at each crash point.

evidence.message: The lifecycle criteria include NTFS, APFS and ext4 crash checks, randomized state transitions and refusal of a second writer.
Relinking, direct client access and recovery are verified. The combined shared-log workflow and crash checks can now run.
All three clients read the same records after restart. A repeated operation wrote once. Isolated tests passed at all three crash points on each OS.

chips.title: Apply the chosen rule for unanswered decisions
chips.summary: If D4 allows defaults, reserve an eligible default once after checking authority and preconditions. If D4 requires waiting, verify that dependent work waits.

evidence.message: An answer that arrives first wins. An unused claim expires without an answer or an effect. The exact eligibility rules come from D4.
D4 allows narrow reversible defaults and calls for authorized panel advice before larger technical defaults.
Eligible local defaults reserve one grant. Tests cover panel declarations, answers arriving first, changed basis, ownership, release and expiry.

chips.title: Handle answers that arrive after a default
chips.summary: If D4 permits defaults, distinguish confirmation, correction before work starts and disagreement after an effect. Preserve both decisions and reconcile any redo.

evidence.message: Verify keep, redo and stale outcomes. A redo needs a fresh grant tied to the state the first action left. Close this item as inapplicable if D4 rules out defaults.
Late disagreement is logged and shown in the next review. Keeping issues no grant. Redo uses the later answer and checks the state left by the default.

chips.title: Export decisions safely for public review
chips.summary: Export selected decisions with redaction. Check fixtures and exports for generic leaks in CI and apply the private deny-list locally before publishing.

evidence.message: The lifecycle privacy contract requires redacted exports. Later project decisions should go through UTP and produce a public decision record.
Selected decisions export with private fields omitted and known sensitive text redacted. Tests cover the deny-list and CI checks fixtures and public records.

chips.title: Classify the evidence used to test review quality
chips.summary: Classify 60 cases as machine-detectable, policy or adapter behavior, or human judgment. Have the person confirm a sample of at least ten before writing fixtures.

evidence.message: The verification plan requires separate test methods for these groups. Only anonymized, reviewed fixtures belong in the public project.
Classified all 60 cases. UTP presented a ten-case sample for confirmation before fixtures are written.
Rewrote the ten-example review in plain language after the reviewer found it unclear. The revised question still needs an answer.
Verified 60 cases. Of these, 21 are machine-detectable, 23 test policy or adapter behavior, and 16 need human judgment. The revised ten-case sample awaits confirmation.
The reviewer confirmed all ten cases on the review page. Four can be checked from the request, three test policy or adapter behavior, and three need human judgment.

chips.title: Complete templates and answers for the selected kinds
chips.summary: Implement D1’s selected kinds in the terminal, including scoped approvals and each kind’s required fields. Track any kinds deferred to phase 2.

evidence.message: Choice and approval templates already exist. Check the selected scope against manual steps, clarification, result checks, assumptions and informational notices.
D1 selected all seven everyday kinds for phase 1.
All seven templates pass terminal tests. Scoped approvals show each option’s authority, and manual steps, result checks and assumptions save per-item answers.

chips.title: Enforce request structure and explain heuristic warnings
chips.summary: Extend the structural checks by request kind. Add heuristics for missing definitions, weak evidence and unclear scope. Show each rule, fix hint and allowed waiver.

evidence.message: Structural rules cannot be waived. Every waived heuristic must show its reason on the card. Train rules on the designated development half.

chips.title: Measure lint on cases the rules were not trained on
chips.summary: Create anonymized before-and-after fixtures after sample confirmation. On the held-out set reach 80% recall and 90% specificity. Report precision and the test mix.

evidence.message: Keep the seven successful cases and five rewritten requests as must-accept examples. Include fresh drafts from all three platforms in the evaluation.

chips.title: Show complete, consistent reviews in Markdown and the terminal
chips.summary: Render the review intent, dependencies, definitions, options and consequences, recommendation, waivers and kind-specific fields. Preserve IDs, revision and custom answers.

evidence.message: AC4 requires every selected kind to pass renderer conformance. A channel that cannot show required content falls back to a complete rendering.

chips.title: Capture review feedback and timing
chips.summary: Save optional clarity feedback, sureness, chosen or custom answers, presentation and answer times. Measure active response time only on channels that observe it.

evidence.message: The concept distinguishes time spent answering from time since presentation and tracks recommendation overrides by choice category.
The terminal and page save optional ratings. Checks covered batch timing, feedback after restart and the absence of timing for piped answers.
Cards explain what they address. A clarification request keeps the choice open and releases any unused default.

chips.title: Use prior decisions when choosing whether to ask
chips.summary: Apply the four asking levels, show relevant reversals, cite existing authorization and save the level and reason. Verify an authorized action proceeds within its original scope.

evidence.message: AC6 requires a prior reversal to reach the agent deciding a related question. The current engine already finds reversals by tag.
Lookup finds related reversals and records the asking level. Tests used a prior verified answer within its exact scope and refused a wider effect.

chips.title: Deliver one notification for each review
chips.summary: Group waiting cards, show open requests in the existing open-items list and route notices with a review or the daily report. Retrying delivery must not send a second notification.

evidence.message: Decision D6 retained these integrations. Use the review ID to deduplicate delivery and show dependent notices with consequential decisions.
Retry and report import tests passed. Live delivery waits for a verified answer covering credential access and the installed morning report.
Decision D6 set one notification per review. The reviewer confirmed that choice and requested one lasting link to all open questions.

chips.title: Provide sandbox setup and a reliable resume path
chips.summary: Show the network setting each platform needs and apply it after confirmation. Verify an external answer resumes the same request and an unreachable service returns exit code 32.

evidence.message: Phase 1c calls for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity runs in their default restricted environments.
Codex, Claude sandbox runtime and Antigravity reached the private service. A separate terminal answered and the original request resumed.

chips.title: Verify presentation and answers on the selected channels
chips.summary: Apply D5’s routing. Distinguish preparation from presentation and acknowledgement. Check chat quotes where available and route consequential approvals to a verified channel.

evidence.message: Bind the answer to the card and revision shown. Test ambiguous assent, intervening corrections, narrower custom approval and overlapping reviews.
D5 requires proof that batches of three or more use the review page.

chips.title: Connect Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity to the CLI
chips.summary: Ship thin platform instructions for asking, independent work, lookup, batching, answering and resuming. Each adapter uses the same request and answer format.

evidence.message: Script the full lifecycle in PowerShell, Git Bash, zsh and bash over SSH, including cancellations, grant recovery and late answers where D4 permits them.

chips.title: Close changed work with evidence for every goal
chips.summary: Produce completion reports that map each goal to evidence and include pending notices. The optional Claude Code Stop hook requests a missing report from the agent.

evidence.message: AC5 requires at least three real tasks with file changes to close this way without waiting for the person to accept routine work.

chips.title: Review a batch and its previews on one page
chips.summary: Ship one page with previews and one save for batches of three or more in phase 1. Test presentation receipts, local page access and revision binding.

evidence.message: Rich review includes page access checks, complete content, stable option IDs and explicit custom answers. Preserve the terminal path.
D5 moves the batch review page into phase 1. Terminal review remains available.
Chrome rendered three cards and an image preview at two widths and saved one batch. Tests cover Host, Origin, token and stale revision checks.

chips.title: Support blind comparisons and the chosen migration
chips.summary: Hide authors and recommendations until a ballot is saved. Refuse identical candidates and changed second ballots. Move existing workflows to UTP in phase 2.

evidence.message: D1 sets the release phase for blind judging. D6b separately decides whether existing comparison workflows move to UTP.
D1 and D6b place side-by-side blind comparisons and migration of the existing comparison workflows in phase 2.
Browser comparison tests and a migration dry run passed. The live migration waits for phase 2, after the first release.

chips.title: Prove the first release on real tasks
chips.summary: Run at least five real tasks across all three agents. Check 80% clarity, duplicate questions, review frequency, notification counts and the waiver rate in the first 15 requests.

evidence.message: Close AC1–AC6 with evidence, including waivers at or below 10%, three completion reports and the shared-tag lookup. Add page or blind tests here if selected for phase 1.
Phase 1 must prove the batch review page on a review with three or more cards.

chips.title: Confirm all everyday kinds shipped in phase 1
chips.summary: Verify that all seven everyday request kinds shipped in phase 1, as D1 selected.

evidence.message: D1’s narrow option moves manual steps, clarification, acceptance and assumptions into the next release. Check the accepted scope for notices as well.
D1 assigned all seven everyday kinds to phase 1. Close this item when their renderers and templates are delivered.

chips.title: Add native question dialogs with complete fallbacks
chips.summary: Map supported native dialogs to stable answer IDs. Preserve consequences and custom replies. Use Markdown or terminal review when a dialog drops content or preselects advice.

evidence.message: Phase 2 calls for capability checks on each platform and conformance for recommended approvals, narrower options and declined actions.

chips.title: Verify rich review with real judgments and handoffs
chips.summary: Run a real blind comparison and a real manual handoff, then verify renderer conformance for every available channel and each delivered kind.

evidence.message: The phase 2 exit criteria require both real reviews and channel conformance.

chips.title: Revisit a decision when its basis changes
chips.summary: Present the original basis and the change. Record keep, amend or reverse, and make the revision discoverable in later lookups.

evidence.message: The phase 3 revisit card applies to a decision whose evidence or preconditions changed.

chips.title: Report observed decisions, reversals and interruptions
chips.summary: Compare real use with the retrospective baseline. Count silent reversals, separate open 30-day windows and report feedback, overrides, waivers, delays and scope mismatches.

evidence.message: Use the measure definitions and their observation windows. Report only measures backed by data and retain the distinction between active response time and delivery time.

chips.title: Version templates and adopt a change from a retrospective
chips.summary: Present the retrospective’s proposed change as a choice. Record the accepted template or policy revision and compare later results with the earlier version.

evidence.message: Phase 3 exits after the first accepted change. The concept also proposes testing an independent choice before showing advice on hard-to-reverse decisions.

chips.title: Answer reviews from the phone inbox
chips.summary: Connect the existing inbox to the shared log. Verify one batch notification, correct answer binding and the 24-hour text purge. Ship when real use shows it saves time.

evidence.message: Decision D6 keeps the phone inbox as a phase 4 answer channel. The service retains the durable record.

chips.title: Offer reviews through the Model Context Protocol
chips.summary: Return answers through MCP elicitation while preserving the full card and its revision. Keep terminal fallback available and ship when a real workflow saves time.

evidence.message: Phase 4 is conditional on demonstrated time savings. The concept places consequences and evidence alongside the elicitation form.
